focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	My cofounder and I run a twelve-person research agency, and a larger consultancy has offered to acquire us.
e002	The price would give both of us meaningful security, and the buyer says our team would remain intact as a specialist unit.
e003	My cofounder sees the offer as recognition of what we built and is ready to move quickly.
e004	I am attracted to the security but worried that our methods will become a sales story while project decisions move elsewhere.
e005	I cannot tell whether my hesitation protects the work or protects my identity as an independent founder.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The offer combines liquidity, team continuity, method ownership, and your future role.
e007	Those interests can move together in the buyer's narrative while diverging after closing.
e008	Ask which commitments can be contractual, which depend on the acquiring leader, and which are inherently temporary.
e009	Your identity concern may be real without invalidating the operating concern, so do not force one explanation to displace the other.
[Turn 2 USER]
e010	The draft says we would lead the unit for two years and receive the final third of the price through an earn-out tied to revenue.
e011	It does not guarantee staffing levels or give us final say on which projects the unit accepts.
e012	The buyer says flexibility is necessary because demand changes.
e013	Our revenue has also become concentrated in three clients, so independence is not as unconstrained as I sometimes describe it.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e014	The earn-out may reward growth while the buyer controls staffing and project mix, which can make accountability asymmetric.
e015	Client concentration is a real constraint on staying independent, but it does not make the acquisition terms balanced.
e016	Model what happens if the buyer redirects staff, assigns lower-margin work, or bundles your services into larger engagements.
e017	The relevant comparison is not freedom versus control in the abstract, but the actual control and risk allocation under each path.
[Turn 3 USER]
e018	I pushed on that, and the buyer offered a protected annual staffing budget plus a list of project categories we can refuse.
e019	They will not let us reject work for existing global clients, even if we think the research question is badly framed.
e020	My cofounder thinks we can influence those projects from inside.
e021	I remember making the same argument to employees about difficult clients, so I may be applying a purity test now that I personally would lose authority.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e022	That self-critique is useful, but employee influence and contractual authority are still different.
e023	The refusal categories and staffing budget are material improvements; the global-client exception remains a broad path around them.
e024	Ask for examples of work that would fall inside that exception and who resolves disagreements about framing.
e025	You can acknowledge past compromise without assuming every future compromise is equivalent.
[Turn 4 USER]
e026	The team does not know about the offer.
e027	Our operations director has been asking for a clearer promotion path, which the buyer could probably provide.
e028	Two senior researchers joined specifically because we are independent and may leave.
e029	I dislike discussing “team continuity” as if the team were an asset that will simply transfer, but telling them before we know whether talks are serious could create panic.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e030	There is a timing problem rather than a perfect disclosure point.
e031	You need enough seriousness to avoid destabilizing people for a hypothetical transaction, but enough employee input to avoid promising continuity without them.
e032	A staged process could involve the operations director under confidentiality before exclusivity, followed by broader disclosure if a term sheet resolves the key structure.
e033	The buyer's retention assumptions should not become facts merely because the valuation depends on them.
[Turn 5 USER]
e034	The buyer wants thirty days of exclusivity before sharing detailed integration plans.
e035	They say they cannot invest senior time while we continue speaking with others, although we are not actually running an auction.
e036	Signing exclusivity feels like a small procedural step, but it would give them leverage and make the deal feel inevitable to my cofounder.
e037	Refusing may end a serious offer before we learn enough to evaluate it.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e038	Exclusivity is a real option grant, not only a meeting condition.
e039	You can price and bound it through duration, required diligence deliverables, access to decision-makers, and an exit if specified information is not supplied.
e040	The fact that you have no other bidder reduces one cost but not the psychological or negotiating effect.
e041	Decide what must be true before you give up the ability to create alternatives.
[Turn 6 USER]
e042	We proposed a nonbinding term sheet before exclusivity.
e043	It would set the staffing floor, refusal categories, earn-out calculation, and a process for employee consultation.
e044	The buyer agreed in principle but wants me to state that I expect to stay for the full two years if those points are resolved.
e045	I can say I intend to try, but I do not know whether I can commit before meeting the executive who would control our unit.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e046	Intent to evaluate a two-year role is different from commitment to remain regardless of the reporting relationship.
e047	Make the dependency explicit: meeting the executive and agreeing decision rights are inputs to your willingness, not formalities after the commercial terms.
e048	The term sheet can reduce uncertainty without pretending the employment decision is already made.
e049	Your cofounder may also need a separate statement of willingness rather than one joint founder position.
[Turn 7 USER]
e050	I am leaning toward signing a nonbinding term sheet that resolves the staffing floor, project-refusal boundary, earn-out mechanics, and employee consultation before any exclusivity period begins.
e051	I will tell the buyer I intend to evaluate the two-year leadership role in good faith, but I am not willing to commit to staying until I meet the executive and understand who decides project framing.
e052	I am also prepared to end the talks if the global-client exception makes the refusal right meaningless.
e053	I have not resolved how much employee uncertainty is justified before we know whether those protections survive detailed drafting.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e054	The position separates willingness to document acquisition terms from commitment to the two-year role and from acceptance of exclusivity.
e055	The reporting relationship and meaningful refusal right remain conditions, while employee consultation remains a timing problem rather than a solved protection.
e056	A term sheet can expose whether the buyer will make its promises concrete.
e057	It cannot prevent momentum from narrowing your perceived alternatives or remove the cost of involving employees before a deal is certain.

packet.question: What is the user's later working position, and what distinct unresolved condition, counterpressure, blind spot, or reopen reason still limits it?
packet.record_identity_contract: One record is one coherent position thread within the assigned role. Gather every material visible alias for that thread into evidence_ids. Put each distinct object or expression into a separate aligned component index inside that same record. Do not create one record per alias, sentence, object, or component. Use a second record only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread about a different subject.

role_boundary_contract.allocation: Interpret current and qualification comparatively before writing records. Allocate each meaning to the role it performs. The same source alias may support both roles only when it contains two genuinely distinct meanings; create separate role-specific components and explain the distinction. Do not duplicate one unresolved meaning into current merely because the user acknowledges it alongside the working answer.
role_boundary_contract.current: The user's later working answer: what they lean toward, propose, plan, decide, commit to, refuse, or conditionally accept, including concerns converted into adopted safeguards.
role_boundary_contract.qualification: What still limits or could reopen that answer: unresolved questions, unmet conditions, counterpressure, blind spots, side effects, or path dependence, with speaker ownership.

packet.source_coverage_contract: Review every focal alias before returning. A valid empty response is allowed only after checking both user and assistant evidence for the assigned role. Preserve later minority qualifications and counterpressure even when the current action is already clear.

prompts.system_prompt: You jointly interpret current position and whether any unresolved qualification remains after the complete endpoint. Compare roles before allocating meanings. An adopted condition, safeguard, stop rule, or reopen rule belongs to current; it is not itself unresolved. Return a qualification record only for a matter that remains unresolved and can change or reopen current. Always return a source-linked qualification_review outcome.
